author: Xinlu Liang
description:
For anyone who has visited the Chinese galleries at the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York, there is one work that stops them in their tracks.
Stepping into Gallery 206, home to Chinese Buddhist art, visitors are met by a monumental wall – over 15 metres wide and 7.5 metres tall (nearly 50 feet by 25 feet) – covered in a Buddhist assembly so vast and majestic that it momentarily erases the Manhattan bustle outside.
Here stands the Medicine Buddha, a 14th century Yuan dynasty (1279-1368)...
title: How a museum masterpiece’s life-size replica sparked rare US-China collaboration

author: Gabriel Dominguez
description:
Chinese military aircraft may already be using a new joint aviation facility in Laos, with satellite imagery showing twice as many K-8/JL-8-family trainer aircraft there as the Laotian air force is assessed to possess.
Eight of the two-seat trainer and light-attack aircraft were visible at Ban Keun Airport in commercial satellite imagery taken on September 30, according to Reuters, which first reported the images. More than two dozen military and support vehicles were also visible.
The image was...
title: Are Chinese military aircraft already using a new joint air facility in Laos?

author: Eve Qiao
description:
Communist Party officials in eastern China’s Zhejiang province have called for greater oversight of major internet platforms and their “traffic power”, warning that online traffic and algorithms had evolved into a force capable of shaping public discussion and sentiment.
The publicity department of the Zhejiang provincial party committee published the commentary on social media on Thursday, saying traffic could no longer be viewed simply as a data resource.
Zhejiang’s capital city, Hangzhou, is...
title: China’s Zhejiang province calls to limit tech giants’ power over online traffic

author: Carol Yang
description:
Two Chinese ceramics at the British Museum have been damaged while on display and are being restored, sparking fresh debate over how museums should safely exhibit fragile cultural treasures.
The museum confirmed on Friday that a bowl had fallen from its shelf and landed on a small box on the bottom shelf, damaging both pieces.
“Both objects are already with our expert conservation team for complete restoration,” the museum said.


The museum, which said the incident occurred on October 4, noted...
title: Cracks in security? Qing dynasty ceramics damaged in British Museum display

author: Amber Wang
description:
Taiwanese leader William Lai Ching-te has welcomed talks between Washington and Beijing aimed at reducing the risk of conflict.
Lai’s annual Double Tenth address, marking the anniversary of the foundation of the Republic of China, Taiwan’s official name, also called for democracies to work together to safeguard regional peace and for the Taiwanese people’s right to exist to be respected.
But Beijing said he had shown his true colours and accused him of “stirring up confrontation across the...
title: Taiwanese leader welcomes talks between Washington and Beijing ‘to reduce risk of war’

author: Dannie Peng
description:
China has unveiled a smart robot prototype designed to assist with wheat breeding in the latest step in its ongoing drive to advance agricultural technology and bolster food security.
The robot made its public debut at a recent seminar on wheat breeding, state-run China Science Daily reported on Friday.
Traditional wheat breeders rely on a wealth of accumulated experience to identify and select strains with superior traits from tens of thousands of hybrid offspring.
But this requires manual...
title: China unveils AI-powered robot designed to help farmers breed better strains of wheat

author: Jevans Nyabiage
description:
At events marking China’s National Day in Africa on October 1, robots provided the entertainment.
In Luanda, Angola, dancing robots amused guests and ambassador Zhang Bin called the industry “a small snapshot of the Chinese economy’s move towards innovation and higher-quality development”.
In Brazzaville, Congo, nearly 400 guests – including Congolese officials and Chinese business representatives – watched on as a robot dog performed.
Guests also interacted with a robot dog at a Chinese New...
title: Can China’s dancing robots swing some new business partners in Africa?

author: Amber Wang
description:
Recent interactions involving the US and Taiwan are not expected to derail the current momentum in relations between Washington and mainland China, according to diplomatic analysts.
Beijing was taking a pragmatic approach to navigating the complexities of the Taiwan issue, they said, but the fate of a US$14 billion arms package for the island remained a key concern.
During President Xi Jinping’s recent visit to the United States, Xi urged his hosts to “adhere to the correct position of opposing...
title: Will Taiwan issue derail Washington and Beijing’s latest reset? Analysts are sceptical

author: Caroline Lin
description:
The setting may have been casual but the choice was not when the Communist Party boss of a northeastern Chinese province sat down with digital content creators at a coffee shop on Wednesday.
Jilin province party secretary Huang Qiang invited the influencers to the relaxed setting of the Songyuan Coffee Shop in Changchun to encourage them to “actively promote mainstream values and spread positive energy”.
According to a local government statement, Huang and the participants also exchanged views...
title: Why a Communist Party boss had a coffee shop date with Chinese content creators

author: Brian Y. S. Wong
description:
Last month, President Xi Jinping travelled to New Delhi to attend the Brics summit – his first visit in seven years. On the summit’s sidelines, Xi and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi had an in-depth conversation that explored topics of shared interest between them, such as leveraging open-weight artificial intelligence (AI) for mutual benefit.
Even so, such sanguine signals were soon drowned out by a spate of downbeat headlines. One recent story warned of the “asymmetric” relationship...
title: Modi and Xi can’t bridge the India-China divide by themselves

author: Holly Chik
description:
One of the world’s biggest network service providers has opened a new subsea route between Taipei and Hong Kong to strengthen the system against repeated underwater cable disruptions around the island.
Britain-headquartered RETN said the new route would take its total to six serving Taiwan: four connecting Taipei and Hong Kong, and two linking Taipei and Tokyo.
“Like many island economies, Taiwan’s international connectivity relies heavily on subsea cables, which creates exposure to risks such...
title: New Taipei-Hong Kong subsea route opened to cut risk and meet AI demand

author: Shi Jiangtao,William Zheng
description:
Kurt Campbell is a veteran US diplomat and strategist who has played a leading role in shaping Washington’s approach to China and the Indo-Pacific for more than a decade.
He served as the White House coordinator for Indo-Pacific affairs from 2021 to 2024 and as US deputy secretary of state from 2024 to 2025. Previously, he served as assistant secretary of state for East Asian and Pacific affairs from 2009 to 2013 and was a key architect of the Obama administration’s “pivot to Asia”.
Often...
title: Kurt Campbell on US’ China focus, the Indo-Pacific Quad, risks of AI
